scores.evidence: The screen-flow diagram (s2-b4) uses flowchart TD, has 3 nodes and short labels, and stays readable at 390 px and in the EN version (desktop-en-10). The two 2-column tables (s2-table, s5-b2) and the term definition blocks (s1-defs, s2-defs, s5-defs, s3-defs) fit at 390 px with no clipping (mobile-jp-07, mobile-jp-09).

No screen is text-only in any of the three runs. Paragraphs are short and broken up by a callout, a table, a prompt or a check about every half screen. Desktop JP is a median 37 chars per line (target 30-40) and EN is a median 71 (target 60-75).

No Japanese is left in the EN screenshots: diagram labels, table headers, prompts and quiz options are all in English (desktop-en-04, -06, -10, -11). The JP screenshots have no stray English beyond the intended terms (MoSCoW, MVP, Must/Should/Could/Won't). The figure has a 'describe in words' toggle, contrast looks fine, and nothing is hidden under the 56 px top bar or the 60 px bottom bar on mobile.

niceToHave: q9 (check-quiz, question 5 of 6) wraps a single 「う？」 onto its own line on desktop JP (desktop-jp-13). Shortening the stem, for example by cutting 「直し方として、」, would avoid the orphaned character.
desktop-en lines reach 78 chars at most, a little over the 75 target, though the median of 71 is fine. Optional: tighten the longest EN paragraph in s5-b1 / hook-b1 if a reflow is wanted.
reader: on mobile the flashcard hint says 「クリックまたはスペースキーでめくる」 (mobile-jp-23). On a touch device it should say tap (タップでめくる).
reader: on mobile the prompt block's 'Claude Codeで使う' button sits next to コピー and stays visible; worth checking that it does something useful on a phone.
summary: The hard-failure checks in metrics.json are all clean: no sideways overflow, no console, Mermaid or image errors, no unknown blocks and no text-only screens. Tables, the TD screen-flow diagram and the prompts are readable at 390 px, and the EN version is fully localized. Nothing has to be fixed; the only lesson-side polish is the orphaned 「う？」 in the q9 stem on desktop JP.
